releases.name: v0.16.31 — Reviewer transform recovery
releases.body:
# v0.16.31 — Reviewer transform recovery

Fix the critical v0.16.30 failure where retained Reviewer correction transforms can run before the configured role materializes, causing OpenCode to disable the entire Sortie plugin and remove Operator recovery tools.

- Keep projection failures inside a fail-closed alias; confirm actual native replay before selecting it.
- Defer unavailable cold restoration while retaining the original role, current model and recovery identity.
- Preserve surrounding deny/ask rules, session permissions, cumulative accounting and single settlement.
- Keep parent status/prompt/context usable even when both correction projection and role restoration fail, with actionable diagnostics. Child-local errors and explicit cancellation failures remain visible.

PR: https://github.com/zufall-upon/Sortie-dogs/pull/404

Source commit: `b58267b9cf8d3c7280333d876360577242aab7cc`

Runtime marker: `0.16.31-reviewer-transform-recovery-v1`

Archive SHA-256: `1c2de0866c185dd62d1298097c4039b9d236cb11994c082e6f2f04b4d3d17eef`

The final source passed full validation and independent source Review after correction of one Medium finding. Linux and Windows CI passed. The fixed archive passed isolated preflight and actual native registry replay/recovery checks. A real CLI Worker started on `openai/gpt-6.1-terra#max`. All 275 bundled files at each of three existing installation locations and eight runtime assets were checked, with settings and explicit model selections preserved.

These checks do not prove recovery of an already-running user session. No shared-host restart, repeated location reload, original-task execution, published-version replacement or old-archive overwrite was performed. A host retaining the earlier failed plugin state still needs a separately authorized or user-performed reload before its loaded version and actual recovery can be verified.

releases.name: v0.16.30 — Git snapshot and Operator recovery
releases.body:
# v0.16.30 — Git snapshot and Operator recovery

## Changes

- Support bounded filesystem snapshots of legitimate shared Git object stores without running Git against writable alternates or weakening metadata validation.
- Preserve safe, actionable failure categories when a registered check cannot bind its source and candidate.
- Resume settled pre-execution process defects with the same plan while retaining Mission results and cumulative budgets.
- Preserve direct validation registration after authorized write-scope expansion, including initially read-only units and older multi-unit records.
- Compare working-directory maps independently of JSON key order and clean up owned test-fixture writers after parent cancellation.
- Align the patch version and runtime marker for ordinary updates from the earlier preparation candidates.

Integrated changes: #397, #398, #399, #400, #401 and #402.

## Fixed package

- Source commit: `d71b9c0c7b57cbbcfebbac89093d5d2bf034f497`
- Runtime marker: `0.16.30-multi-scope-recovery-v1`
- SHA-256: `4159a1b44a9f9149bcfb474b7f885055179c070c820cef083e6cb9cd2dc488a4`

The attached archive is the previously validated candidate, not a repack. Candidate preflight, final full validation, and Linux/Windows CI passed. The same 275 bundled files were verified at all three existing installation locations, with eight runtime assets and explicit settings preserved. The final review correction was validated and self-rechecked by its author; that is not a separate independent final PASS.

Installed bytes and isolated Worker startup do not prove that an already-running host has loaded the update or that a paused real project has recovered. Reload the host separately and verify its loaded version before resuming its formal checks. Previously published packages and earlier candidate archives are not replaced.

releases.name: v0.16.27 — Git review boundaries
releases.body:
# v0.16.27 — Git review boundaries

- Mission review and snapshot inventory harden Git metadata handling, worktree comparisons, filters, fsmonitor and submodule inspection (#384).
- Scoped alternate-index `git add` and Git command parsing receive focused boundary fixes. The separate Windows snapshot-console change is included (#387).
- The README distinguishes the v0.17.x test-optimization vision from implemented, measured behavior (#388).
- Candidate preflight model expectations and temporary-path handling were corrected (#390, #391).

Release commit: `f09be34e2a9f68a7e970d6403f5880de24f0e19d`.
Archive SHA-256: `c73c3207571c008905f699c1f6940750049ea0befd5cdd934df40220a9d80adb`.
Runtime marker: `0.16.27-git-review-boundaries-v1`.

The integrated candidate passed the full test command and the commit's Linux and Windows CI checks. An isolated CLI probe observed a Worker session starting on `openai/gpt-6.1-terra#max`; that observation is not task completion or an official score. A running OpenCode host must be restarted manually before its loaded version can be confirmed.

# v0.16.26 — Nested validation scratch

## Changes

- Resolve explicitly configured validation scratch relative to the individual check's working directory, including a nested checkout. Generated scratch no longer invalidates that check solely because its directory differs from the Location.
- Continue to protect declared inputs, tracked inputs, and exact outputs. Refresh and Review rediscover tracked inputs for the captured validation working directory, including newly tracked files; older bindings keep their original scratch recipe.
- Reuse the scoped tracked-file discovery from #384 and disable `core.fsmonitor` for those scans. A Git subdirectory Location still scans its own tracked files even when its `.git` is in an ancestor.

The execution recovery, validation evidence, Coordinator default and concise reports from #384 were already delivered in #385 and v0.16.25; they are not reapplied here. The older stale-evidence record did not retain a per-file snapshot diff, so this change does not establish its unique cause.

## Review disposition and deferred work

- #384's tracked-file protection finding for a Git subdirectory Location is valid; the Location scan is retained and covered alongside the nested-checkout cases.
- Its fsmonitor finding applies to the introduced tracked-file scans; the existing #384 override is included for these scans, without claiming to secure all Git operations.
- The `.git/info/attributes` compatibility finding concerns #384's private filterless Review implementation, which is not included here; that implementation's behavior is neither adopted nor claimed fixed.
- The redirected-metadata and nested Git Review content findings, the recursive submodule/filterless Review work, and broader Git hardening remain deferred. The user did not request that work as a condition of this integration. The pre-existing behavior and the synthetic reproduction described in the v0.16.25 notes are not claimed fixed.

## Release identity

The Mission runtime asset marker is `0.16.26-nested-validation-scratch-v1`. After integration, fix the `main` commit and a single SHA-256-pinned archive for candidate preflight, full validation, applicable CI, CLI Worker startup, installation and distribution. Worker startup is not task completion or an official score. npm publication is a separate manual step; an installed marker alone does not prove that a running host has reloaded it.

# v0.16.25 — Execution and validation recovery

## Changes

- Recover eligible predecessor execution evidence and reconcile native terminal state, validation binding and writer ownership without forcibly releasing a live or unknown owner.
- Keep validation scratch exclusions tied to the individual check and preserve declared and Location-tracked inputs. A cwd-relative scratch exclusion not present in the earlier Location-relative recipe is deferred, so generated files in such a nested checkout may make a check stale.
- Recognize quoted Git identity values without weakening command-boundary checks.
- Default the Mission Coordinator to Terra while retaining explicit model overrides and existing role configuration.
- Keep the normal return report concise while retaining its summary, cost and history caveats, and internal records.

The historical stale-evidence record did not retain a per-file snapshot diff, so its unique cause is not established. Execution recovery does not establish completion or official grading of an external task.

## Deferred Git behavior

This candidate retains the published Location-only snapshot Git scan rather than the new nested-checkout scan, and does not include the later recursive submodule Review implementation. The earlier Review path for ordinary nested Git checkouts remains. A synthetic run with a writable nested checkout and its `.git` redirected to another host-readable repository produced that repository's tracked content in `missionReviewSource`'s excerpt in v0.16.24. Actual host permission bypass, real secret disclosure and external transmission were not established by that internal-function reproduction. The collection behavior and broader Git-boundary work remain for follow-up; this is not a claim that the behavior is safe.

## Release identity and validation

The Mission runtime asset marker is `0.16.25-execution-recovery-v1`. Record the integrated `main` commit and one SHA-256-pinned archive for candidate preflight, full validation, Linux/Windows CI and actual CLI Worker startup. Worker startup is not task completion or an official score. Use the same fixed archive for installations and the GitHub Release; npm publication is a separate manual step. An installed marker does not prove that a running OpenCode host has reloaded the plugin; verify its loaded path and marker after a manual restart.
